name: Example: Finding Higher-Order Derivatives
problem: Evaluate $g_{xyz}(x,y,z)$ at $(1,2,3)$ if $g_x(x,y,z) = 2x y z +  y^3.$
worked_solution:
First, we find $g_{xy}(x,y,z)$ by differentiating $g_{x}(x,y,z)$ with respect to $y\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}_{xy}(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2xyz+{y}^{3}) \\  & =2xz+3{y}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find $g_{xyz}(x,y,z)$ by differentiating $g_{xy}(x,y,z)$ with respect to $z\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}_{xyz}(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂z}(2xz+3{y}^{2}) \\  & =2x\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}_{xyz}(1,2,3) & =2(1) \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$
